The goal of this vignette is to replicate the analysis of PBC data
performed by [@Vavra-etal2024] using package **clustGLMM**.
This is the list of packages required for the analysis:

```{r pacakges}
library("survival")
library("mixAK")
library("clustGLMM")
```

## PBC910

The sequential PBC data can be found as `pbcseq` in package
`survival`.  We restrict ourselves only to patients who survived the
first 910 days (2.5 years) similarly as [@KomarekKomarkovaJSS14mixAK],
who created `PBC910` in package `mixAK`.  However, we need more
columns than `PBC910` provides so we create our data from objet
`pbcseq` by taking the same rows as `PBC910`.

```{r pbc-data}
data("PBC910", package = "mixAK")
data("pbc", package = "survival")
data <- merge(PBC910, pbcseq, by = c("id", "day", "platelet", "spiders"))
dim(data)
(n <- length(unique(data$id)))      # number of subjects in the data
```

Next we prepare the outcomes for analysis:

```{r data-transformations}
data$ord_edema <- factor(data$edema, ordered = TRUE)
data$lalbumin <- log(data$albumin)
data$time <- data$day/365.24
data$age <- data$age / 10
```

The analysis in the paper consisted of 

* numeric serum bilirubin and albumin (both on log-scales),

* binary indicators of blood vessel malformations in the skin
  (`spiders`) and presence of hepatomegaly or enlarged liver
  (`hepato`),

* ordinal `edema` (0 = no edema, 0.5 = untreated or succesfully
  treated, 1 = edema despite diuretic therapy).

We create the `family` argument to declare the type of the considered
outcomes for analysis with `clustGLMM`:

```{r family}
family <- c(lbili = "num", lalbumin = "num", 
            spiders = "bin", hepato = "bin",
            ord_edema = "ord")
```

The formulas for analysis are the same for all outcomes.  The fixed
effects part is an additive model with linear effect of `time`
and `age` adjusted for different `sex`.  All these effects are assumed
to be group-specific.  Finally, outcomes are joined via random
intercepts.

```{r formula}
formula <- list()
for (y in names(family)) {
  formula[[y]] <- list(fixed = ~ 1, # will become ~ 0
                       group = ~ time + age + sex,
                       random = ~ 1)
}
```

Below we show the summary of the variables considered within this
analysis:

```{r data-summary}
summary(data[, c("time", "age", "sex", names(family))])
```

We see that some of the outcome values are missing.  However, for
`clustGLMM` there is no need for omitting the rows from the analysis
as long as the missing values are among modelled outcomes.

Now we examine how does the outcome evolve in time:

```{r plot-pbc-vs-time}
layout(matrix(c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 
                3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 0.5))
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "lbili", x = "time", id = "id")
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "lalbumin", x = "time", id = "id")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "spiders", x = "time", main = "spiders")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "hepato", x = "time", main = "hepato")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "ord_edema", x = "time", main = "ord_edema")
```

## Sampling MCMC using `clustGLMM`

Some of the key inputs for `clustGLMM` are already prepared (`family`,
`formula`), but there are still some key settings to be specified.
Non-effects parameters of the model may also be set to be
group-specific.  The default setting is provided by

```{r varying}
(varying <- default_varying())
```

Only the precision of the errors of numeric outcomes and ordered
intercepts are considered to be group-specific parameters by default.
We set the precision matrix (`InvSigma`) of the vector of random
intercepts to be group-specific as well, but keep its Wishart prior
scale matrix `InvQ` common to all groups.  Missing outcome values will
be always predicted for the current cluster the individual is assigned
to.

```{r varying-InvSigma}
varying["prec_num"] <- TRUE
varying["InvSigma"] <- TRUE
```

Next, we can choose which parameters are returned.  We make just one
change compared to the default setting and that is to save the
predicted missing values.

```{r save}
save <- default_save()
save["naY"] <- TRUE
```

For `tuning` we will use settings that and `param` will be kept
without any changes.

```{r tuning}
tuning <- default_tuning(experience = TRUE)
param <- default_param(sparse = FALSE)
param$prec_num_rte <- 1
```

Since we do not know the number of underlying clusters in advance, we
set the maximal number of clusters `G` to 5.  We also apply
standardization of covariates and outcomes to ensure that priors are
truly non-informative.  We run a couple of randomly initialized chains
for initial 1000 iterations.

```{r clustGLMM-burnin}
G <- 2
set.seed(123456789)
mcmc_burnin <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = "id", family = family, data = data,
                         G = G, nchains = 2, iter = 2000, 
                         varying = varying, save = save, tuning = tuning, param = param,
                         standardize = TRUE)
```

The default `plot` output informs us about the evolution of number of
patients within each cluster separately for all chains:

```{r plot-mcmc-burnin}
plot(mcmc_burnin)
```

The current chains cannot be used for inference.  We continue to
sample from initial values set to `mcmc_burnin$last` and sample
$10\,000$ iterations.

```{r clustGLMM}
mcmc <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = "id", family = family, data = data,
                  G = G, nchains = 2, iter = 10000, 
                  inits = mcmc_burnin$last,
                  varying = varying, save = save, tuning = tuning, param = param, 
                  standardize = TRUE)
```

```{r plot-mcmc}
plot(mcmc)
```

```{r plot-mcmc-clusters-kde}
ch <- 1
plot(mcmc, "beta_num", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_bin", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_ord", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "c_ord", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "sdSigma", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "corSigma", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "w", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
```

```{r post-processing}
mcmc_pp <- post_processing(mcmc)
```

```{r Uclustering}
data[, "Uclustering"] <- mcmc_pp$clustering[as.character(data$id), ch]
```

```{r plot-pbc-vs-time-clustered, fig.height = 6}
layout(matrix(c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 
                3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 0.5))
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "lbili", x = "time", group = "Uclustering", id = "id")
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "lalbumin", x = "time", group = "Uclustering", id = "id")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "spiders", x = "time", group = "Uclustering", main = "spiders")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "hepato", x = "time", group = "Uclustering", main = "hepato")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "ord_edema", x = "time", group = "Uclustering", main = "ord_edema")
```

```{r summary}
mcmc_pp_summary <- summary(mcmc_pp)
print(mcmc_pp_summary, which = "clust_param")
print(mcmc_pp_summary, which = "group_param")
print(mcmc_pp_summary, which = "inv_param")
```

```{r}
clustering <- with(data |> dplyr::filter(!duplicated(id)),
                   table(Uclustering))
clustering
prop.table(clustering)
fit <- survfit(Surv((fu.days - 910) / 365.25, status == 2) ~ Uclustering,
               data |> dplyr::filter(!duplicated(id)))
plot(fit, col = 1:2,
     xlab = "Follow-up period after day 910 [years]",
     ylab = "Survival probability")
```
